key_insight: Stoichiometry-preserved ionic clusters, paired with pretrained MLIPs and multi-task fine-tuning, can predict detonation velocity for multi-ionic energetic materials before full crystal structures are known.
engineering_relevance: This offers a synthesis-facing screening route for data-scarce materials discovery, reducing the need for exhaustive crystal-structure prediction while still leveraging physically grounded atomistic models.
method: Non-periodic stoichiometric ionic-cluster representation for each candidate material
Pretrained MLIP backbone fine-tuned with multi-task energy-force regularization
Cross-validated screening of curated perovskite-type energetic materials and transfer to unseen ABX4 compounds
evidence_signal: On 25 curated PEMs with experimental K-J detonation velocities, the model achieved cross-validated screening performance and transferred to three newly synthesized ABX4 materials with a reported MAE of 92 m·s^-1 without retraining.
watch_item: Performance depends on sparse, curated labels and may be sensitive to how well the cluster representation captures unseen chemistries or packing effects outside the training distribution.
paper_title: Stoichiometric cluster learning for few-shot property prediction of multi-ionic integrated energetic materials
